transcript.text: How do you decide what to focus on when
everything feels urgent?
>> It's a prioritization issue, not an
urgency issue. So, imagine a pilot has a
you know, a cabin light that's
flickering while they're landing with
one engine. Okay, well, we see that we
need to change the bulb here, but
there's also a one engine that's on
fire. We should focus on that, not the
flickering light. Like if you go to the
emergency room, it's literally called
triage. Okay, do you have a broken ankle
or do you have a heart attack? Broken
ankle, you can stay here. Heart attack,
go straight in. And so, fundamentally
like you have limited resources and so
you have to be able to prioritize and
you have to let fires burn. We have to
accept the fact that there's going to be
problems, they're going to occur, the
business will never be perfect, and we
have to say that's okay.
